senses.definition_en: food that is served with tortillas

examples.english: Niña Chole, however, had a great virtue: she felt compassion for the misery of others. She was poor herself, but for those even poorer, she always showed mercy. […] “Do you have a spare little tortilla, niña Chole?” “No; but hold on. I'll prepare one for you.” Or another day: “You see, I only had enough for food, but not for tortillas.” “Take these two roughly-made tortillas, maybe they’ll do you good.”
examples.ref: 2007, Francisco Andrés Escobar, “La niña Chole”, in El país de donde vengo, LibrosEnRed, →ISBN, page 14:
examples.text: La niña Chole, sin embargo, tenía una enorme virtud: se compadecía de la miseria ajena. Ella era pobre, pero, para los todavía más pobres, siempre tenía un gesto de misericordia. […] “¿No lia sobrado alguna tortillita, niña Chole?”. “No; pero perate. Ya te la vuechar”. U otro día: "Fíjese que solo mialcanzó para el conqué”. “Tomá estas dos chengas, a lo mejor te caen bien”.
examples.translation: Niña Chole, however, had a great virtue: she felt compassion for the misery of others. She was poor herself, but for those even poorer, she always showed mercy. […] “Do you have a spare little tortilla, niña Chole?” “No; but hold on. I'll prepare one for you.” Or another day: “You see, I only had enough for food, but not for tortillas.” “Take these two roughly-made tortillas, maybe they’ll do you good.”

examples.english: Salvadorans are the children of maize; from maize they make their tortillas, which can never be lacking; the Salvadoran primarily subsists on tortillas — everything else is just the the rest (of food), which is served with them. Many families survive solely on tortillas with a pinch of salt, or with spicy chili to trick hunger.
examples.ref: 2016 September 23, Francisco Martínez Criado, “Suchitoto. Julio 2009” (chapter 1), in Las cenizas del comal, Lacre, →ISBN, page 18:
examples.text: Los y las salvadoreñas son los hijos e hijas del maiz, de maíz hacen sus tortillas que nunca pueden faltar; el salvadoreño se alimenta básicamente de tortillas, lo demás es el conqué, que le acompaña. Muchas familias se alimentan exclusivamente de tortillas con un puñado de sal, o con chile picante para engañar al hambre.
examples.translation: Salvadorans are the children of maize; from maize they make their tortillas, which can never be lacking; the Salvadoran primarily subsists on tortillas — everything else is just the the rest (of food), which is served with them. Many families survive solely on tortillas with a pinch of salt, or with spicy chili to trick hunger.
